d3-sankey: Sankey charts (src/kit/chart.ts). SVG draws the picture, but no browser API lays out a flow: placing the nodes in columns and relaxing the links so they cross least is the library's whole job.
fflate: The link codec and every zip (src/kit/codec.ts, src/kit/zip.ts). CompressionStream has no preset dictionary, which makes short documents 20 to 35 percent smaller, is asynchronous, and writes a gzip stream, not a zip archive (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx, Download everything).
leaflet: The Trip Planner's map (src/apps/trip/editor.ts). The browser has no map: panning and pinch-zooming a grid of OpenStreetMap tiles, with markers and a route, would be a library written here instead. Loaded only with the Trip Planner.
lit: Every element's drawing (the kit and the editors). Custom elements are native; lit adds the drawing of a template again with only its changed parts, which the browser does not do, and reactive properties that ask for it.
lucide: The icons (src/kit/icons.ts). The browser has no icon set and emoji draw differently on every system; Lucide is SVG paths, each a module, so only the icons used are built in and the rest come as a lazy chunk with the picker.
mathjs: The Calculator's units, big numbers and algebra (src/apps/calc/math.ts). The browser's only expression reader is eval, which the page's policy forbids, and Intl formats units without converting them. A custom build, in the Calculator's chunk alone.
@axe-core/playwright: The accessibility checks in e2e/a11y.spec.ts. Chromium exposes its accessibility tree but no rules to judge it by; axe is the rule set. Tests only.
@playwright/test: The end-to-end runner (e2e/). node:test has no browser; WebDriver BiDi is a protocol, not a runner, and WebKit at phone size is what an iPhone gets. Tests only.
@types/d3-sankey: Types for d3-sankey, which ships none. Not built into the site.
@types/leaflet: Types for leaflet, which ships none. Not built into the site.
@types/node: Types for the scripts and tests that run under node. Not built into the site.
@vitest/browser-playwright: Lets Vitest run the DOM tests in a real Chromium through Playwright (test/browser/, src/apps/*/tests/). A simulated DOM would pass what a browser fails. Tests only.
playwright: The browsers themselves (Chromium, WebKit) for the browser tests and e2e, pinned to @playwright/test's version. Tests only.
typescript: The type check (npm run lint), and its scanner reads the source for the lints of the code (test/lints.ts: the words in templates, the module graph). Node strips types natively and runs the scripts as written, but checks none of them, and has no tokenizer for TypeScript. Not built into the site.
vite: The build. Browsers load ES modules unbundled, but a page per app, hashed file names the offline copy can trust, lazy chunks per editor, minified code and the CSP's script hashes are a build's work. Not built into the site.
vitest: The unit and browser tests. node:test runs the unit tests' shape but not in a browser; one runner for both layers keeps one way to write a test. Not built into the site.
wrangler: Deploys the three Workers and runs them locally (npm run deploy, tinier:dev, media:dev). Cloudflare's REST API could, by hand; wrangler is Cloudflare's own tool for it. Not built into the site.
prettier: The one style of the code (npm run format writes it, npm run lint checks it: .prettierrc is single quotes, lines to 200, templates left as written). Node has no formatter, and a style held by hand drifted with every builder. Not built into the site.
fast-check: The properties fuzzed from TLO's grammar (test/doc/tlo-grammar.ts, test/doc/properties.test.ts): generators of documents, texts and operations, and shrinking a failure to its smallest case; and the random walks over the chrome (test/browser/walks.test.ts, its model-based testing: fc.commands and asyncModelRun). The native alternative is nothing: no browser or node API generates or shrinks test cases. Tests only.
